title: Maps to a constant group scheme are clopen decompositions
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an abelian group, and let $T_E=\coprod_{e\in E}T$ be the constant group scheme over $T$, with coprojections $\iota_e:T\to T_E$, components $V_e=\iota_e(T)$, structure morphism $\pi:T_E\to T$, sum $f+g$ of $T$-morphisms and canonical map $e\mapsto c_e$ as in [def-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme] (a $T$-scheme in the sense of [def-weil-scheme-over-base]). For every object $s:U\to T$ of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], giving a $T$-morphism $f:U\to T_E$ is equivalent to giving a family of pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes $(U_e\subseteq U)_{e\in E}$ whose union is $U$: the bijection sends $f$ to $(f^{-1}(V_e))_{e\in E}$, and its inverse sends $(U_e)$ to the unique morphism $f$ with $f|_{U_e}=\iota_e\circ s|_{U_e}$ for all $e$ (only finitely many $U_e$ are nonempty when $U$ is quasi-compact). Equivalently it is a map $\varphi:|U|\to E$ whose fibres are open and closed (equivalently, open), namely $\varphi_f(x)=e\iff f(x)\in V_e$. Under this equivalence, the canonical map $E\to h_{T_E}(U)=\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,T_E)$, $e\mapsto c_e=\iota_e\circ s$, sends $e$ to the morphism with $U_e=U$ and $U_{e'}=\varnothing$ for $e'\ne e$, hence to the constant map with value $e$; and the group law is pointwise addition: $\varphi_{f+g}=\varphi_f+\varphi_g$. In particular $f\mapsto\varphi_f$ is an isomorphism of $\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,T_E)$, with the sum of [def-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme], onto the abelian group of maps $|U|\to E$ with open fibres under pointwise addition, and $e\mapsto c_e$ is a group homomorphism. (The etaleness of $U\to T$ is not used: the statement holds for every $T$-scheme $U$.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5), using Groupoids, Example 39.5.6 (Tag 03YW) for the constant group scheme and its decomposition into copies of the base

proof.text: *Step 1 (the components of $T_E$).* By [def-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], $T_E=\coprod_{e\in E}T$ with coprojections $\iota_e$ that are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]; the sets $V_e=\iota_e(T)$ are open, pairwise disjoint and cover $T_E$, so each $V_e$ is also closed (its complement $\bigcup_{e'\ne e}V_{e'}$ is open). The structure morphism satisfies $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_T$. Since $\iota_e$ is an open immersion, it is an isomorphism $\iota_e':T\xrightarrow{\sim}V_e$ onto the open subscheme $V_e$ followed by the inclusion $j_e:V_e\hookrightarrow T_E$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 26.14.1 (Tag 01JB, lemma-glue) with $U_{ij}=\varnothing$ for $i\ne j$: $X=\bigcup U_i$, $U_i\cap U_j=\varphi_i(U_{ij})=\varnothing$

proof.text: *Step 2 (from a morphism to a clopen decomposition).* Let $f:U\to T_E$ be a $T$-morphism, i.e. $\pi\circ f=s$. Put $U_e=f^{-1}(V_e)$. Since $f$ is continuous and the $V_e$ are open (Step 1), each $U_e$ is open; since the $V_e$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $T_E$, the $U_e$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $U$; hence $U\setminus U_e=\bigcup_{e'\ne e}U_{e'}$ is open and $U_e$ is open and closed. We regard $U_e$ as an open subscheme of $U$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 26.14.1 (Tag 01JB, lemma-glue), second mapping property, $g\mapsto V_i=g^{-1}(U_i)$, with $V_i\cap V_j=g^{-1}(U_{ij})=\varnothing$

proof.text: *Step 3 (the restriction of $f$ to $U_e$ is forced).* With $f$ and $U_e$ as in Step 2, $f(U_e)\subseteq V_e$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] there is a unique morphism $f_e:U_e\to V_e$ with $j_e\circ f_e=f|_{U_e}$; put $h_e=(\iota_e')^{-1}\circ f_e:U_e\to T$, so $\iota_e\circ h_e=f|_{U_e}$. Applying $\pi$ and using $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_T$ (Step 1) and $\pi\circ f=s$ gives $h_e=\pi\circ\iota_e\circ h_e=\pi\circ f|_{U_e}=s|_{U_e}$. Hence $f|_{U_e}=\iota_e\circ s|_{U_e}$ for every $e\in E$: a $T$-morphism $U\to T_E$ is determined by the decomposition $(U_e)$ (the only $T$-morphism $U_e\to T$ is $s|_{U_e}$).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 26.14.1 (Tag 01JB, lemma-glue), second mapping property: $g_i=\varphi_i^{-1}\circ g|_{V_i}$; Schemes, Lemma (Tag 01HI, lemma-restrict-map-to-opens) for the factorization

proof.text: *Step 4 (from a clopen decomposition to a morphism; the bijection).* Conversely let $(U_e)_{e\in E}$ be pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes covering $U$. The morphisms $\iota_e\circ s|_{U_e}:U_e\to T_E$ agree on the overlaps $U_e\cap U_{e'}$, which are empty for $e\ne e'$; so by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] there is a unique morphism $f:U\to T_E$ with $f|_{U_e}=\iota_e\circ s|_{U_e}$ for all $e$. It is a $T$-morphism: $(\pi\circ f)|_{U_e}=\pi\circ\iota_e\circ s|_{U_e}=s|_{U_e}$ for every $e$, so $\pi\circ f=s$ by the uniqueness part of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Moreover $f^{-1}(V_e)=U_e$: $f(U_e)\subseteq\iota_e(T)=V_e$, and $f(U_{e'})\subseteq V_{e'}$ is disjoint from $V_e$ for $e'\ne e$, while the $U_{e'}$ cover $U$. Thus the composite (decomposition $\mapsto$ morphism $\mapsto$ decomposition) is the identity; and the composite (morphism $f\mapsto (f^{-1}(V_e))\mapsto$ glued morphism $f'$) is the identity because $f$ and $f'$ both restrict to $\iota_e\circ s|_{U_e}$ on every $U_e$ (Step 3), so $f=f'$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. This is the asserted bijection between $\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,T_E)$ and the clopen decompositions of $U$ indexed by $E$. Nothing here uses that $s$ is etale.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 26.14.1 (Tag 01JB, lemma-glue), second mapping property $\Mor(Y,X)$ for the glueing data with $U_{ij}=\varnothing$ ($i\ne j$), whose proof the source omits; written out here

proof.text: *Step 5 (maps with clopen fibres; finiteness).* A family $(U_e)_{e\in E}$ of pairwise disjoint subsets covering $U$ is the same as a map $\varphi:|U|\to E$, via $U_e=\varphi^{-1}(e)$ and $\varphi(x)=$ the unique $e$ with $x\in U_e$; the $U_e$ are open and closed iff the fibres of $\varphi$ are. If all fibres are open they are also closed, since $U\setminus\varphi^{-1}(e)=\bigcup_{e'\ne e}\varphi^{-1}(e')$. For $f$ as in Step 2 the map is $\varphi_f(x)=e\iff f(x)\in V_e$. If $U$ is quasi-compact, the open cover $(U_e)_{e\in E}$ has a finite subcover $U_{e_1},\dots,U_{e_n}$; a nonempty $U_e$ with $e\notin\{e_1,\dots,e_n\}$ would be disjoint from all $U_{e_k}$ and hence not covered, so only $U_{e_1},\dots,U_{e_n}$ can be nonempty.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5): sections are the Zariski locally constant maps $U\to G$

proof.text: *Step 6 (the canonical map).* For $e\in E$ the canonical map gives $c_e=\iota_e\circ s$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme]. Then $c_e(U)\subseteq V_e$, so $c_e^{-1}(V_e)=U$ and $c_e^{-1}(V_{e'})=\varnothing$ for $e'\ne e$ (the $V$'s are disjoint); thus the decomposition of $c_e$ is $U_e=U$, $U_{e'}=\varnothing$, and $\varphi_{c_e}$ is the constant map with value $e$.

source.place: Groupoids, Example 39.5.6 (Tag 03YW), with Etale Cohomology, Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5)

proof.text: *Step 7 (the group law is pointwise addition).* Let $f,g:U\to T_E$ be $T$-morphisms, $P=T_E\times_TT_E$ with projections $p,q$, and $(f,g):U\to P$ the morphism with $p\circ(f,g)=f$, $q\circ(f,g)=g$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; it is a $T$-morphism and $f+g=m\circ(f,g)$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme]. For the components $W_{e,e'}=p^{-1}(V_e)\cap q^{-1}(V_{e'})$ of $P$ we get $(f,g)^{-1}(W_{e,e'})=f^{-1}(V_e)\cap g^{-1}(V_{e'})=\{x:\varphi_f(x)=e,\ \varphi_g(x)=e'\}$. By the definition of $m$ [lem-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme-multiplication] (b), (c), $m(W_{e,e'})\subseteq V_{e+e'}$; since the $W_{e,e'}$ cover $P$ and the $V$'s are disjoint, $m^{-1}(V_d)=\bigcup_{e+e'=d}W_{e,e'}$. Hence $(f+g)^{-1}(V_d)=\bigcup_{e+e'=d}\{x:\varphi_f(x)=e,\varphi_g(x)=e'\}=\{x:\varphi_f(x)+\varphi_g(x)=d\}$, i.e. $\varphi_{f+g}=\varphi_f+\varphi_g$. The maps $|U|\to E$ with open fibres form an abelian group under pointwise addition (the fibre of $\varphi+\psi$ over $d$ is the union of the open sets $\varphi^{-1}(e)\cap\psi^{-1}(d-e)$; the fibres of $-\varphi$ are those of $\varphi$; constants have open fibres). Since $f\mapsto\varphi_f$ is a bijection (Steps 4, 5) carrying $+$ to pointwise addition, $\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,T_E)$ with $+$ is an abelian group and $f\mapsto\varphi_f$ is a group isomorphism; by Step 6, $e\mapsto c_e$ corresponds to $e\mapsto$ (constant map $e$), which is additive.
